result.title: AGQ: Action-Guided Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models
result.comment: 3 figures, 3 tables. Code and experimental results: https://github.com/Qiuxu00/AGQ
result.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform tasks specified through natural-language instructions, but their large weight footprint challenges deployment on memory-constrained onboard platforms. Ultra-low-bit quantization reduces this footprint, yet preserving task performance and controlling weight recovery costs remain challenging. We propose Action-Guided Quantization, which combines action sensitivity with a measured proxy for weight recovery cost to allocate matrix bitwidths under storage budgets. Per-channel calibration compensates for quantization error, while a uniform bitwidth within each matrix preserves regular layouts. Bit-dependent grouped lossless coding reduces resident weight storage, and block-wise recovery limits temporary buffers. On LIBERO, AGQ achieves 92.7% task success at W3, exceeding AWQ and GPTQ by 1.2 and 3.7 percentage points, respectively, and retains 70.5% success at W2.5. An asymmetric configuration, denoted W1.5$^{*}$, uses W4 vision weights and a parameter-weighted average of 1.5 bits for language weights. With lossless coding, it achieves $6.10\times$ complete-model compression relative to BF16 while retaining 25.5% task success. Code and experimental results are available at https://github.com/Qiuxu00/AGQ

AI.brief_summary: 面向 VLA 模型部署，提出以 action 敏感度和权重重构代价为依据的矩阵位宽分配与超低位量化流程，并在 LIBERO 上报告压缩率与任务成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 属纯权重压缩与部署效率工作，不涉及 latent 状态生成、视觉证据使用或推理期决策；action 敏感度虽被用作位宽分配代理，但仅作用于权重通道，与 LVR 的状态、贡献分配问题缺少可直接借鉴的联系。
